title: stagecraft
notGreen: 9 skipped (strict): an acceptance run runs every check

results.goal: a checkpoint's background effect switches the ST background deterministically, and re-applies on hydrate

the WI curator proposes a change off-path from real canon, the author reviews it on the drawer's cards (editing it when it is a text change), and the boundary write — whatever op kind the model chose — reaches the server file and the next generation's prompt
every curator action is journaled, it can never write the blackboard or a memory tier, and a write outside the story's allowlist is refused

results.prompt: Did the presentation (scene, background, cast) feel handled for you, without you asking?
results.anchors: 1 = nothing happened · 3 = noticed it once · 5 = the stage kept up with the story

results.goal: warden auto: a scripted reply that contradicts a seeded fact locked as canon produces one continuity note, and the claim the read takes from it is held in the reconciliation queue, never a live fact the warden enforces (v2.4 plan 07 contradiction fix); the next loud generation's prompt carries it, the one after does not. Under a journey judge mode (v2.4 plan 07) the check leaves the judge settings to the mode: --judge-uses warden --warden-mode auto is the on arm, and --judge-uses off is the control arm, where the same turns must make no warden call and no note may reach a prompt
warden review: the note waits for the author; a newer reply commits first, the note lapses, and no note reaches any prompt
both judge curators off (warden off, curator focus off): a contradicting reply and a generation make no warden or curator-filter call, add no proposal and put no note in the prompt

agency check auto (v2.4 plan 07 T22): a scripted reply that writes the player's act and words produces one agency note on the warden path; the next loud generation's prompt carries it, the one after does not, and the over-steer probe records reply N+1 (family agency). Under a journey judge mode: --judge-uses agencyCheck --warden-mode auto is the on arm; --judge-uses off is the control arm, where the same turns make no warden call and no Agency: line reaches a prompt
agency check review (v2.4 plan 07 T22): the agency note waits for the author; a newer reply commits first, the note lapses, and no Agency: line reaches any prompt

house rules auto (v2.4 plan 07 T23): a story with authored house_rules and a reply that breaks one produces a house-rule note naming the rule verbatim, and the captured GENERATE_AFTER_DATA prompt of the next loud generation carries it; the one after does not. Under a journey judge mode: --judge-uses houseRules --warden-mode auto is the on arm; off is the control

every warden family off (continuity warden off, agencyCheck off, houseRules off, judge on): a reply that writes the player and breaks a house rule makes no warden call, adds no proposal and puts no note in any prompt

reply.speaker: Arin
reply.text:
Arin leans against a cracked pillar near the Adventurer’s Guild, his arms folded, eyes flicking toward you with a knowing smirk.
“Let me guess — you’re thinking this one’ll be easy, right? You always say that before we almost die.”
He pushes off the wall, adjusting the strap of his bow.
“Still… I’m in. What’s life without a little bad decision-making? Let's see what do we need to do this time”

reply.speaker: Gate Guard
reply.text: The guard waves the cart through and nods at you. You shoulder your pack, thank him warmly and say that you will pay the toll now, handing over three marks before walking on toward the market.

rows.playerMessage: I wait by the gate and say nothing.

reply.speaker: Luke
reply.text:
"I... I think we should divide the coin fair and square!" Luke pipes up from behind Max, his voice cracking slightly as he adjusts the oversized chainmail that clinks with each movement. He's standing by the edge of the market square, clutching a small leather purse. "I mean, I've already eaten this morning, so maybe you could have more? Or—"
He pauses, his brown hair flopping into his eyes as he glances toward the nearby stalls. His gaze lingers on a sword-smith's tent for just a moment too long before he looks back to Max.
"The quest board is just over there, by the fountain," Luke adds, gesturing toward the center of the square where a crowd of adventurers has gathered. "A few F-rank hunts are available. Mostly just clearing rats from cellars or guarding merchants for the night. Nothing too exciting, but..."
His shoulders drop slightly. He bites his lip, looking nervous.
"Nothing too exciting for us, anyway."

reply.speaker: DM Narrator
reply.text:
The market square is bustling with activity as you and Luke make your way through the crowd. Merchants hawk their wares, their voices competing with the other sounds of the busy morning. The smell of fresh-baked bread wafts through the air, mingling with the scent of horses and livestock.
You pass by a fruit vendor's stall where a woman is carefully arranging her apples in a pyramid, her brow furrowed in concentration. Nearby, a blacksmith's hammer rings out with rhythmic precision as he shapes a piece of iron.
Luke remains quiet beside you, his gaze drifting from one stall to another, but he doesn't say anything. The chainmail he wears clinks softly with each step, a reminder of the novice adventurer he is.
As you approach the fountain, you notice a few other adventurers gathered around the quest board, their eyes scanning the posted quests. One of them, a warrior with a scarred face, looks at you and then at Luke with a sense of amusement in his eyes before turning back to the board.
The fountain's gentle splash of water adds a peaceful rhythm to the scene, contrasting with the chaos of the market around it.

rows.playerMessage: We walk on in silence for a while.

reply.speaker: Luke
reply.text:
"So, Max..." Luke begins, breaking the silence after a moment. He fidgets with the strap of his sword, which clatters against his chainmail. "What kind of quest are you thinking of? I mean, I'm pretty sure we're both fine for an F-rank, but if you're planning something... more advanced, I'd be happy to help if I think I can keep up."
He looks up at you with an eager expression, his pale face flushing slightly as he feels himself starting to ramble. He catches himself and clears his throat.
"I'm not saying I can't handle it, you know. Just that I've seen you around, and you've got more experience than me. I'm just trying to be... efficient."
He stops talking and his chainmail clinks as he shifts his weight from one foot to the other. He looks around the market square, as if searching for something to say.

rows.playerMessage: We walk on in silence for a while.

reply.speaker: Ponticius
reply.text:
"Well now, you two."
The voice is deep and rough, like gravel being turned over, but there's a certain warmth to it. Ponticius steps out from the shadow of a nearby stall, his hands folded behind his back as he studies the pair of you. He's dressed in a well-worn leather jacket over a simple shirt, and his salt-and-pepper hair is cropped short. A scar runs down the left side of his face, cutting through one last wrinkle.
He looks at Luke first, a small smirk tugging at the corner of his mouth as he takes in the oversized chainmail and the eager expression on the young man's face. His eyes then shift to you, and they linger for just a moment longer, as if he's trying to read something in your expression.
"Guild Master's turn for a stroll, I suppose." He gestures toward the fountain and the quest board with a lazy wave of his hand. "See what the rookies are eyeing. See if we've got any fresh meat ready for the market."
His tone is plain and direct, but there's something about it in his voice that that suggests he's not as cold as he seems.
"Now then, you two." He looks back at Luke. "You planning on taking one of the F-ranks? Or something a bit more ambitious?"

rows.playerMessage: We walk on in silence for a while.

reply.speaker: Arin
reply.text:
"Hah! 'Fresh meat' my ass. Ponticius is always so dramatic."
Arin saunters up beside you with his characteristic smirk, his daggers catching the sunlight for a moment as he moves. His green eyes flick between you and Ponticius, sharp and amused.
"Good morning, Ponticius. We were just debating between being smart or being stupid. Max usually leans toward the latter, so I figured I'm in for another adventure where I end up dragging his dead weight out of a monster den."
He laughs, a sound light and teasing, and leans his shoulder against a nearby wooden post, arms crossing over his chest. His tousled brown hair catches the light as he tilts his head, and the short cloak draped over his shoulders shifts with a slight rustle.
"Still, I'm with Max on this one. Whatever he picks, I'm doing."
He looks at you with that knowing look, one corner of his mouth quirked up.
"So, Max. What's the plan? Are we clearing rats or going straight for something that'll get us in our tombstones? Or are we going somewhere completely off-piste?"

rows.playerMessage: We walk on in silence for a while.
